title: Finite coproducts of coherent topoi are componentwise coherent
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set and let $(\mathcal E_i)_{i\in I}$ be Grothendieck topoi, with small-site presentations $\mathcal E_i\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_i)$ in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Sites and sheaves of sets have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Define the disjoint-union site $\mathcal C$ to have objects $(i,U)$ with $U\in\mathcal C_i$, morphisms $(i,U)\to(i,V)$ the morphisms $U\to V$ of $\mathcal C_i$, no morphisms between different components, and coverings exactly the coverings within a component. Put $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. Restriction to the components gives an equivalence $\mathcal E\simeq\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal E_i$. Under it, limits, colimits and epimorphisms are componentwise. The geometric morphism $j_i:\mathcal E_i\to\mathcal E$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism] has inverse image $(A_k)_k\mapsto A_i$ and right adjoint placing $A_i$ in component $i$ and the terminal object in every other component. These morphisms exhibit $\mathcal E$ as the coproduct $\coprod_i\mathcal E_i$ of topoi: a family of geometric morphisms $u_i:\mathcal E_i\to\mathcal F$ induces $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, unique up to the compatible natural isomorphism, with
$$u^{-1}A=(u_i^{-1}A)_i,\qquad u_*(B_i)_i=\prod_i u_{i,*}B_i,\qquad uj_i\simeq u_i.$$
This construction is independent of the presentations up to equivalence. If every $\mathcal E_i$ is coherent in the sense of [def-trf-coherent-topos], then $\mathcal E$ is coherent, and an object $(A_i)_i$ is coherent if and only if every $A_i$ is coherent. For $I=\varnothing$ the construction is the degenerate topos with one object and one arrow.

source.place: Agent formulation of the finite coproduct construction from Definition 00VH (definition-site), the set-sheaf equalizer condition 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets), limits 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf) and colimits 00WI (lemma-colimit-sheaves); the coherence assertion uses the explicit quasi-compact/quasi-separated definitions in def-trf-coherent-topos. These sources supply the construction tools, rather than a named coproduct-coherence theorem.

proof.text: A presheaf on the disjoint-union site is exactly a tuple of presheaves on the component sites: every object and arrow has a unique component and there are no cross-component morphisms. The sheaf equalizer condition is checked separately on each covering family, so restriction and tuplewise extension give mutually inverse equivalences $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_i)$. The same description computes limits, colimits and epimorphisms componentwise. For the empty finite index set there is one presheaf and one sheaf, hence the terminal category. This is the direct construction from the sheaf equalizer, limit and colimit definitions in the cited Stacks tags.

source.place: Tags 00VH and 00VM, with limits 00W2 and colimits 00WI; direct disjoint-union construction.

proof.text: Under the product equivalence, the projection to the $i$-th component is left exact. Its right adjoint sends $A_i$ to the tuple having $A_i$ in component $i$ and the terminal object elsewhere: a morphism from $(B_k)_k$ to this tuple is uniquely a morphism $B_i\to A_i$, since every other component has a unique map to the terminal object. Thus the resulting geometric morphism has the stated inverse image and right adjoint by [def-trf-geometric-morphism].

source.place: Product-category adjunction calculation for the component inclusions.

proof.text: Given geometric morphisms $u_i:\mathcal E_i\to\mathcal F$, define $u^{-1}A=(u_i^{-1}A)_i$. It preserves finite limits componentwise. For a tuple $(B_i)_i$, the object $u_*(B_i)_i=\prod_i u_{i,*}B_i$ is right adjoint because $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal F}(A,\prod_i u_{i,*}B_i)$ is naturally $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E_i}(u_i^{-1}A,B_i)$. The empty product is terminal. The component inclusions satisfy $u j_i\simeq u_i$ by construction, and uniqueness of the adjoint supplies the compatible natural isomorphisms. Hence this is the coproduct universal property of topoi.

source.place: Universal-property calculation for finite products of sheaf categories and geometric morphisms.

proof.text: Replacing any component site by an equivalent site replaces its sheaf category by an equivalent topos. Taking the finite product of these equivalences gives an equivalence between the corresponding product categories, and the disjoint-union equivalences of Step 1 identify the resulting constructions. Thus the construction is independent of the chosen presentations up to equivalence.

source.place: Equivalence invariance of the sheaf-category presentation in Definition 00VH.

proof.text: Assume every component topos is coherent. First, a tuple $A=(A_i)_i$ is quasi-compact exactly when every $A_i$ is quasi-compact. For the forward implication, extend any covering family of $A_i$ to a covering family of $A$ by using identity maps on the other components; a finite subcover of $A$ restricts to one of $A_i$. Conversely, a covering family of $A$ is componentwise epimorphic, so finite subfamilies cover each $A_i$; the union of these finitely many index sets covers $A$. The initial object is quasi-compact by strictness. Next, $A$ is quasi-separated exactly when every $A_i$ is quasi-separated. For the forward implication, put quasi-compact objects over $A_i$ in component $i$ and initial objects elsewhere; their fibre product is quasi-compact, hence its $i$-component is. Conversely, componentwise limits identify a fibre product over $A$ with the tuple of fibre products over $A_i$, which is quasi-compact by the preceding equivalence. Thus $(A_i)_i$ is coherent exactly when every $A_i$ is coherent. This argument uses only [def-trf-coherent-topos] and the strict, disjoint, universal finite-coproduct calculus [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity].

source.place: Definition of quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects in the coherent-topos node, with the strict/disjoint/universal finite-coproduct calculus of Tag 00WI/00WJ.

proof.text: For each coherent component choose its small finite-limit-closed full generating subcategory from [def-trf-coherent-topos] and adjoin the initial object; finite limits involving the initial object remain initial by [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity]. The product of these finitely many enlarged subcategories is small, finite-limit-closed, and consists of coherent tuples by Step 5. It generates the product: for a tuple $(A_i)_i$, take the coproduct of the component-supported tuples having a generator in one component and the initial object in every other component. Its map to $(A_i)_i$ is componentwise epimorphic, because the chosen generators cover each $A_i$. Hence the product topos is coherent. If $I=\varnothing$, the terminal category has its sole object as a small finite-limit-closed coherent generating subcategory.

source.place: Definition of a coherent topos and its generating subcategory, together with the finite extensive coproduct calculus; corrected component-supported generator construction.
